tasks.short: Give emergency medical instructions to callers.

steps.what: Hear the caller describe the medical emergency.
Provide emergency medical instructions to callers.
Stay with the caller until a responder arrives.

tasks.design: The dispatcher hears the caller and provides the emergency medical instructions by voice. No script speaks for the dispatcher, and no tool chooses the instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: The instructions depend on what the caller says in the moment, which a stored card cannot hear.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the need for a person to give those instructions.
tasks.still_hard: The caller may be panicked, the condition may change, and the wrong instruction can harm someone.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher chooses and speaks every instruction. A card on the wall is not a substitute.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. Giving emergency medical instructions stays with the dispatcher for the whole call.

reach.learn: The instructions up to that point were spoken by the dispatcher

evidence.claim: Speaking emergency medical instructions is a decision with an immediate effect on a person, so it stays with the dispatcher.
Classifying an emergency call, or setting its priority, would choose the response without the dispatcher. The dispatcher keeps that decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the caller describes a medical emergency and ends when a responder takes over or the call closes. Dispatching the unit is a separate task.
No fields are generated. The dispatcher speaks from the protocol they are qualified to use. There is no transcript and no model.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. None of the time is counted as saved.
Upkeep is zero because no list or screen step is added.
unknowns: Which medical instructions this service allows a dispatcher to give.
Whether a clinician must join the call for some conditions.
research_questions: Which medical instructions may the dispatcher give under national rules?
When must a clinician join the call?

already_counted.description: Providing the medical instructions stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: No screen or list is added, so there is nothing to keep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case and the centre are the same. The instructions do not shrink, so the saving is zero. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Question callers and determine the response needed.

steps.what: Question callers to determine their locations.
Question the nature of their problems.
Determine the type of response needed.

tasks.design: The dispatcher questions the caller about location and the problem, then determines the type of response. No tool classifies the call or picks the response.
tasks.previous_blocker: The questions change with each answer, so a fixed form cannot run the call.
tasks.enabler_now: The dispatcher can see a map while talking. The questions and the determination stay theirs.
tasks.still_hard: Callers give partial locations, and two problems on one call can need different responses.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher determines the response from the live call. A form does not.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. Questioning callers and determining the response stay with the dispatcher.

reach.task: Attend the response the dispatcher named
reach.learn: The response type was determined by the dispatcher on the call

evidence.claim: Determining the response from a live call is the dispatcher's decision and is not classified by a tool.
Classifying an emergency call, or setting its priority, would choose the response without the dispatcher. The dispatcher keeps that decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the call connects and ends when the dispatcher has determined the response type. Sending the unit is a separate task.
No score and no class label are stored by a model. The dispatcher may type a location later, in the recording task. This task does not record the call audio.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. None of the time is counted as saved.
Upkeep is zero because no classifier and no new list are added.
unknowns: How location is confirmed when the caller cannot name a street.
Which response types this service uses.
research_questions: How does the dispatcher confirm a location the caller cannot name?
Which response types is the dispatcher allowed to determine alone?

already_counted.description: Questioning callers about location stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: No classifier or list is added, so there is nothing to keep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case and the centre are the same. Questioning the caller and determining the response do not shrink, so the saving is zero. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set priorities and dispatch units under procedures.

steps.what: Hear the situation before any unit is sent.
Determine response requirements and relative priorities.
Log the dispatch the dispatcher already made.

tasks.design: The dispatcher determines the requirements and the relative priorities, then dispatches the units by radio under the service's procedures. {OPS_SYSTEM} only logs the dispatch the dispatcher already made. It does not choose a unit or a priority.
tasks.previous_blocker: The radio dispatch was already spoken, and the same units were written again in a book.
tasks.enabler_now: The console can store the unit and the time after the dispatcher has sent them.
tasks.still_hard: Two situations can compete for the same unit, and the procedure still has to be applied by a person.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher sets the priority and dispatches the unit. A log line is not a dispatch.
tasks.altitude: Setting priorities and dispatching units stay with the dispatcher. Only the log of a dispatch they have already made is shorter.

reach.learn: Move only when the dispatcher has dispatched the unit

evidence.claim: A log line can store the unit and the time after the dispatcher has dispatched them.
Classifying an emergency call, or setting its priority, would choose the response without the dispatcher. The dispatcher keeps that decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the response type is known and ends when the log is stored. The radio dispatch itself stays outside any automatic send.
The log fields are unit id, situation id, and the time. The dispatcher produces the unit by dispatching it. Nothing is logged for a unit the dispatcher did not send. Audio is not recorded.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the priority and the dispatch. The log does not set either.
Upkeep is keeping unit ids aligned with the console.
unknowns: Whether the console already writes a log line when the dispatcher keys the radio.
Who may override a priority when two situations compete.
research_questions: Does the console already log a unit when the dispatcher sends it?
Who may change a priority after units have been dispatched?

already_counted.description: Dispatching units stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep unit ids aligned with the console

approvals.approved_version: units the dispatcher dispatched under established procedures

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the console already logs the radio dispatch, the write disappears and the low end is zero beyond the unchanged priority and dispatch. Those two do not shrink in either case. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Receive alarm system calls at the console.
Decide if the call is an emergency or information.
Note the department the caller asked for.
Store the department note the dispatcher accepted.

tasks.design: The dispatcher receives the telephone or alarm call and decides whether it is an emergency or information for police, fire, ambulance, or an after-hours department. {OPS_SYSTEM} stores only the department note the dispatcher accepted. It does not class the call.
tasks.previous_blocker: The call was answered by a person, and the department was written a second time after the call.
tasks.enabler_now: The console can store a department the dispatcher has named, beside the call the console already opened.
tasks.still_hard: Alarm lines, after-hours departments, and a caller who asks for the wrong service all need the dispatcher to hear them.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher decides what the call is. A stored department is not that decision.
tasks.altitude: Receiving the call and deciding what it is stay with the dispatcher. Only a department note they have accepted is shorter to store.

reach.task: Take an after-hours call the desk passed on
reach.learn: Act on a department only after the dispatcher has named it

evidence.claim: A department name the dispatcher has accepted can be stored on the call.
Classifying an emergency call, or setting its priority, would choose the response without the dispatcher. The dispatcher keeps that decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the line rings and ends when the accepted department note is stored. Questioning, priority, and dispatch stay in their own tasks.
The note fields are call id and department. The dispatcher produces the department. A call with no acceptance is not stored as a department. Audio is not recorded.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on receiving the call and deciding what it is.
Upkeep is keeping the list of departments the city still routes after hours.
unknowns: Which departments still receive after-hours calls through this desk.
Whether alarm calls already open a console record before anyone answers.
research_questions: Which city departments does this desk still answer after hours?
Does an alarm already open a console record on its own?

already_counted.description: Deciding whether the call is an emergency stays inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the list of after-hours departments

approvals.approved_version: department note the dispatcher accepted after receiving the call

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If every alarm already opens its own record, the note is smaller and the low end falls. Receiving the call and deciding what it is do not shrink in either case. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Medical instructions, questioning callers, priorities, and dispatching units stay with the dispatcher for the whole call. A log of a dispatch they have already made, or a department they have already named, takes less of a second writing.
reach: A field unit moves when the dispatcher has dispatched it
An after-hours department is named by the dispatcher, not by a classifier
skills_to_grow: Giving medical instructions without a script that speaks for them
Setting priority before any log is written
Receiving the call before it is classed
role.ambitious_version: Every unit that moves was dispatched by the dispatcher, and every log describes a decision they had already made.
